metaSkillRoutingBehavior.actualBehavior: using-agent-skills maps task phase to skill names through a Markdown flowchart and quick-reference table. It relies on host skill discovery via name/description frontmatter; it is not an executable router and does not include capability scoring.

comparisonWithEssa.Navigator: ESSA Navigator is broader: user intent, context, capability routing, product knowledge, approval and response modes.
comparisonWithEssa.CapabilityFabric: ESSA has structured capability contracts and risk/approval policies; Agent Skills has workflow descriptions.
comparisonWithEssa.ExecutionWorkflow: ESSA has explicit execution states, gates and proof artifacts; Agent Skills has human-readable lifecycle workflows.
comparisonWithEssa.TechnologyIntelligence: ESSA has source trust tiers and adoption gates; Agent Skills has internal skill selection rules.

routingIdeasEssaLacks: Simple phase-to-skill quick-reference table for coding work.
Mandatory assumption/confusion surfacing as a meta-skill behavior.
Anti-rationalization tables embedded in each workflow.

developmentLoopComparison.finding: Agent Skills is narrower and engineering-lifecycle-focused. ESSA is broader and governance-first. Agent Skills contributes useful local workflow micro-patterns, not a replacement for ESSA.

gapAnalysis.note: ESSA has strong rules, but not per-workflow rationalization/reality tables.
ESSA proof artifacts, browser proofs and regression lists are stronger.
ESSA has execution, security, approval and proof gates.
ESSA requires tests but not always a recorded RED failure before implementation.
ESSA verifies and fixes regressions, but a named reproduce-localize-reduce-fix-guard protocol is useful.
Codex review stance exists; a formal five-axis pre-merge matrix could improve consistency.
ESSA already has browser proof workflows; upstream security boundary text is useful.
Direct ship/deploy/push authority conflicts unless fully subordinated to ESSA approval.
Useful as a simple Engineering Skill Resolver vocabulary, but ESSA already owns routing.

securityFindings.finding: MIT license verified from GitHub repository metadata and LICENSE file.
Documented install paths include npx, marketplace plugin install, git clone, and tool-specific copy. Direct install would write to agent/plugin config and local skill directories.
Root hooks can execute bash at session start in Claude-oriented environments; one skill contains a runnable bash helper. Codex manifest documents empty hook config for Codex.
Some skills instruct use of external docs, GitHub, DevTools MCP, CI/CD, deployment and monitoring tools. The skill pack itself is mostly Markdown, but workflows can lead to network use.
Skill instructions are external prompt material. Direct adoption increases the prompt/instruction surface and must not override ESSA governance.

Browser DevTools guidance explicitly warns against real browser profile exposure, cookies/localStorage/sessionStorage, and browser-content-as-instructions. This is a documented mitigation, not proof of safety.
Ship, CI/CD and Git workflows can involve commits, tags, push, deployment, production flags and external providers. Direct use conflicts with ESSA's authority boundary unless wrapped.
Marketplace/npx install paths can pull current upstream state. Pinning/version review would be required before future adoption.

promptInstructionSecurity.foundDestructiveCommandInstruction: No explicit malicious instruction found in sampled/targeted files, but git/deployment skills contain legitimate commands that become dangerous without ESSA gates.
promptInstructionSecurity.assessment: External skill instructions must be data for ESSA Technology Intelligence until separately approved. Future adoption must sandbox or rewrite them under ESSA authority.

MODE_A_DIRECT_SKILL_ADOPTION.reason: Would install external prompt material and potentially hooks/scripts into the agent environment. It risks duplicate or conflicting authority with ESSA governance.

MODE_B_PATTERN_EXTRACTION.reason: Extract the useful engineering workflow patterns natively into ESSA while keeping ESSA approval/security/workflow contracts authoritative.

MODE_C_HYBRID.reason: Could use selected upstream skills as optional development tooling, but only under an ESSA wrapper that strips push/deploy/provider/billing/secrets authority and pins reviewed versions.
